currentState: Chapter 7: an older captain and a young clerk-mage, each failed by his own institution and not quite hearing each other. Havel is paternal and dismissive ('Not now, lad.', 'Hear me out, lad.'), keeps Corin's notices unread under the cracked river stone; Corin defers in manner ('Sorry. Captain.') and does not defer in substance: he corrects 'four yards', and twice overrides Havel's timing with paper.
powerDynamic: Havel has rank, ground and men. Corin has the copies, the access and the facts. In the room Corin is right and Havel concedes only the cart point ('The lad's right about the carts. Fair enough.') and then proposes the same plan plus spikes at the gate.

physicalDynamics.pattern: Corin brings his notices to the post himself; Havel leaves them 'with the others'. Corin lifts the river stone off the dusty pile and sets it on his own sheets. At the table Corin keeps his hand flat on the bills and goes pale; Havel goes back to the canvas, then comes round behind Corin to read Sylvanas's sheet, kneading his scarred knuckles.

history.event: Chapter 7: Havel mid-sentence telling Corin to 'leave it with the others'; Corin pulls the stool for Jaina; Corin interrupts Havel's 'four yards' with 'It isn't four yards.'
Chapter 7: 'Forty-one out of how many thousand loads' (Havel) / 'And the forty-one already gone?' (Corin) / 'I can't arrest a village.'
Chapter 7: Corin argues speed on Kett's bills (first carts out); Havel agrees on the carts, repeats his plan with spikes at the gate and the shift-change arrest.

trajectory: Ch7: Corin's paper contradicts Havel's habits; the notice-pile under the river stone is a low-key plant.
